# 12-Week Strength + Hypertrophy Programme

**Client:** 26F, recreational lifter, on COC (no cycle phasing required)
**Start date:** Monday, 1 June 2026
**End date:** Sunday, 23 August 2026
**Structure:** 4 sessions/week — Upper/Lower split with one heavier and one higher-volume day per body region
**Session days:** Mon (Lower A), Tue (Upper A), Thu (Lower B), Fri (Upper B). Wed/Sat/Sun off or light cardio/mobility.

---

## Programme Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Dates | Focus | Avg Intensity | Avg Volume |
|-------|-------|-------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1. Hypertrophy Accumulation | 1–4 | 1 Jun – 28 Jun | Volume, work capacity, technique under load | RPE 6–8 | High |
| 2. Strength Emphasis | 5–8 | 29 Jun – 26 Jul | Heavier compounds, lower reps on primaries | RPE 7–9 | Moderate |
| 3. Peak + Deload | 9–12 | 27 Jul – 23 Aug | Intensification, then test, then deload | RPE 8–9, then taper | Moderate → Low |

Progression: linear load progression within each phase (~2.5% on upper, ~5% on lower compounds week-to-week when reps are hit at target RPE). Accessory work progresses primarily through reps before load.

---

## PHASE 1 — Hypertrophy Accumulation (Weeks 1–4)

### Template

**Lower A (Squat-focused) — Monday**
- Back Squat — 4 × 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Romanian Deadlift — 3 × 8–10 @ RPE 7
- Walking Lunge — 3 × 10/leg
- Leg Press — 3 × 12
- Standing Calf Raise — 4 × 10–12
- Hanging Knee Raise — 3 × 12

**Upper A (Bench-focused) — Tuesday**
- Barbell Bench Press — 4 × 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-Supported Row — 4 × 8–10
- DB Shoulder Press — 3 × 8–10
- Lat Pulldown — 3 × 10–12
- DB Lateral Raise — 3 × 12–15
- EZ-Bar Curl — 3 × 10
- Triceps Rope Pressdown — 3 × 12

**Lower B (Deadlift-focused) — Thursday**

- Hip Thrust — 3 × 10

**Upper B (Press/Pull volume) — Friday**

- Incline DB Press — 3 × 10
- Seated Cable Row — 3 × 10–12
- Face Pull — 3 × 15
- Hammer Curl — 3 × 10
- Overhead Triceps Extension — 3 × 12

### Weekly Progression
- **Week 1 (1–7 Jun):** Establish baseline loads at top of rep range, RPE 7.
- **Week 2 (8–14 Jun):** +2.5% upper, +5% lower on primaries; accessories add 1 rep where possible.
- **Week 3 (15–21 Jun):** Push to RPE 8 on primaries; add a 4th set to one accessory per session.
- **Week 4 (22–28 Jun):** Light deload — primaries 3 × 5 @ ~70% of Week 3 top load, RPE 6; cut accessory sets by ~40%.

---

## PHASE 2 — Strength Emphasis (Weeks 5–8)

Primaries shift to lower-rep, higher-intensity work. Accessories maintain hypertrophy stimulus.

### Template

**Lower A — Monday**

- Romanian Deadlift — 3 × 6 @ RPE 8
- Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat — 3 × 8/leg
- Leg Extension — 3 × 12

- Pull-Up — 3 × 6–8 (add load if possible)
- DB Lateral Raise — 3 × 12
- Incline DB Curl — 3 × 10

**Lower B — Thursday**

- Pause Front Squat — 3 × 5 @ RPE 7
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 × 6/leg
- Glute-Ham Raise (or Nordic) — 3 × 6–8
- Hip Thrust — 3 × 6 @ RPE 8
- Hanging Leg Raise — 3 × 10

**Upper B — Friday**
- Overhead Press — 5 × 4 @ RPE 8
- Weighted Pull-Up — 4 × 5
- Incline Bench Press — 3 × 6
- Chest-Supported Row — 3 × 8
- Cable Lateral Raise — 3 × 12
- Skullcrusher — 3 × 8

### Weekly Progression
- **Week 5 (29 Jun – 5 Jul):** Reset primaries to ~85% of estimated 1RM, RPE 8.
- **Week 6 (6–12 Jul):** +2.5–5% load; same reps.
- **Week 7 (13–19 Jul):** Push to RPE 9 on top set of primaries; aim to add load or 1 rep.
- **Week 8 (20–26 Jul):** Mid-cycle back-off — primaries drop sets by 1 and reduce to RPE 7; accessories unchanged. Not a full deload.

---

## PHASE 3 — Peak, Test, Deload (Weeks 9–12)

### Week 9 — Intensification (27 Jul – 2 Aug)
Primaries:
- Back Squat — Work up to 3 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Bench Press — 4 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Deadlift — 3 × 3 @ RPE 8
- Overhead Press — 4 × 3 @ RPE 8.5

Accessories: as Phase 2, cut to 2 sets each.

### Week 10 — Peaking (3–9 Aug)
- Back Squat — Work up to a heavy double @ RPE 9; back-off 2 × 3 @ 85%
- Bench — Heavy double @ RPE 9; 2 × 3 @ 85%
- Deadlift — Heavy double @ RPE 9
- OHP — Heavy double @ RPE 9

Accessory volume cut ~50%. Sleep and food prioritised.

### Week 11 — Test Week (10–16 Aug)
- **Mon:** Squat 1RM (warm-ups: 5/3/2/1/1, then attempts ~92%, ~97%, 100%+)
- **Tue:** Bench 1RM
- **Thu:** Deadlift 1RM
- **Fri:** OHP 1RM + light pulling

Only 1–2 light accessory sets after tests to keep blood flow without fatigue.

### Week 12 — Deload (17–23 Aug)
Three short sessions, no fourth. Movements: all primary lifts at 60% × 3 × 3, technical focus. Skip most accessories or keep them at 2 × 10 RPE 5. Lots of walking, mobility, sleep.

---

## Warm-Up Protocol (every session)
1. 5 min easy bike or row
2. 5 min targeted mobility (hips/T-spine/shoulders by session focus)
3. Specific warm-up: empty bar → progressive ramp-up sets to working weight (typically 4–5 sets, halving reps as load increases)

## Conditioning (optional, recovery-permitting)
- 1–2 × 20–30 min Zone 2 (incline walk, bike) on off days
- Skip in Week 11; resume light in Week 12

## Recovery & Lifestyle Notes
- **Sleep:** target 7.5–9 h. Non-negotiable in Weeks 7, 9, 10, 11.
- **Steps:** 8–10k/day baseline.
- **RPE calibration:** in Week 1, anchor RPE through video review; recreational lifters routinely under-rate RPE early.
- **Autoregulation rule:** if a top set falls 2+ reps short of target at the prescribed RPE, hold load next session rather than progressing.

## Nutrition (general — adjust to her goal)
The brief didn't specify a body-composition goal. Default recommendation for "build strength and muscle while staying lean":
- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily
- **Calories:** maintenance or slight surplus (+150–250 kcal) through Phase 1–2; maintenance through Phase 3
- **Carbs:** prioritise around training (40–80 g pre, 60–100 g post depending on size)
- **Hydration:** 30–35 ml/kg + ~500 ml per training hour
- COC has no programming implications here, but worth flagging: oral contraceptives can slightly blunt strength gains at the margins in some literature — not a reason to modify the plan, just a reasonable expectation-setter.

## Tracking
Log every working set: load, reps, RPE. Re-test estimated 1RMs informally at end of Phase 1 (Week 4 deload review) and formally in Week 11. Compare bar speed/RPE on matched loads between Weeks 1, 5, and 9 to gauge progress beyond top-set numbers.

# Nutrition Plan — Hypertrophy Support

**Client:** 26F recreational lifter
**Duration:** Aligned to 12-week programme (1 Jun – 23 Aug 2026)
**Goal:** Support muscle growth across all three phases while managing recovery and body composition.

---

## Step 1 — Establish Baseline Numbers

You'll need her current bodyweight to finalise targets. The plan below uses **placeholder values for a 65 kg client** — scale linearly to her actual weight.

### Estimated Maintenance (TDEE)
- Resting Metabolic Rate (Mifflin-St Jeor, age 26, ~165 cm, 65 kg): ~1,420 kcal
- Activity multiplier 1.55 (4 training days + general daily activity ~8–10k steps): **~2,200 kcal/day maintenance**

Validate over the first 7–10 days: weigh-ins each morning (post-void, pre-food), average the week. If weekly average is flat ±0.3 kg, maintenance is accurate. Adjust the surplus from there.

---

## Step 2 — Caloric Targets by Phase

| Phase | Weeks | Kcal Target | Rationale |
|-------|-------|-------------|-----------|
| 1. Hypertrophy Accumulation | 1–4 | **Maintenance + 250 kcal** (~2,450) | Lean surplus to support volume and recovery |
| 2. Strength Emphasis | 5–8 | **Maintenance + 250–350 kcal** (~2,450–2,550) | Slightly larger surplus as intensity rises and joints/CNS take more load |
| 3. Peak/Test/Deload | 9–12 | Wk 9–10: Maintenance + 200 kcal • Wk 11 (test): Maintenance • Wk 12 (deload): Maintenance –100 to –200 kcal | Maintain performance while modestly trimming fat regained during surplus |

Expected weight gain on this plan: **~0.2–0.3 kg per week** in Phases 1–2. Faster than this signals excessive fat gain — drop calories by ~150. Flatlining for >2 weeks means add ~150.

---

## Step 3 — Macronutrient Split

### Protein — Non-negotiable
- **1.8 g/kg bodyweight** daily → **~120 g/day** (at 65 kg)
- Distributed across 4 feedings of ~30 g each, spaced 3–5 hours apart
- One feeding within 1–2 hours pre-training, one within 1–2 hours post

### Fat
- **0.8–1.0 g/kg** → **~55–65 g/day**
- Floor of 0.7 g/kg for hormonal and joint health — don't go below
- Emphasise mono- and polyunsaturated sources; ~1/3 from omega-3-rich foods (oily fish 2–3× week or supplement)

### Carbohydrate — Fills the remainder
- At ~2,450 kcal: ~120 g protein (480 kcal) + ~60 g fat (540 kcal) = leaves **~1,430 kcal for carbs → ~355 g/day**
- This is the training-fuel macro; bias intake around sessions

---

## Step 4 — Daily Distribution (Training Day Template)

Example for a Monday Lower A session at 18:00.

| Meal | Time | Approximate Composition | Notes |
|------|------|------------------------|-------|
| Breakfast | 07:30 | 30 g protein, 60 g carbs, 15 g fat (~500 kcal) | e.g. Greek yoghurt + oats + berries + nuts |
| Lunch | 12:30 | 35 g protein, 80 g carbs, 15 g fat (~650 kcal) | e.g. Chicken, rice, vegetables, olive oil |
| Pre-training snack | 16:30 | 20 g protein, 60 g carbs, low fat (~370 kcal) | e.g. Whey + banana + rice cakes/honey |
| Post-training meal | 19:30 | 35 g protein, 100 g carbs, 15 g fat (~700 kcal) | e.g. Salmon, potatoes, salad |
| Evening snack | 21:30 | 25 g protein, 25 g carbs, 10 g fat (~330 kcal) | e.g. Casein/cottage cheese + fruit |

**Totals:** ~145 g P / 325 g C / 55 g F / ~2,550 kcal — within Phase 2 target range.

### Rest Day Adjustments
- Drop ~50 g carbs (mostly from pre- and post-training meals)
- Keep protein and fat identical
- Net ~2,250 kcal on rest days, ~2,450–2,550 on training days

---

## Step 5 — Peri-Workout Specifics

- **Pre (1.5–2 h before):** 20–30 g protein + 60–80 g carbs, low fat/fibre
- **Intra (optional):** Plain water + electrolytes; if session >75 min or appetite is low, 30 g carbs from a sports drink
- **Post (within 1–2 h):** 30–40 g protein + 80–100 g carbs

Total window-protein matters more than timing precision, but for hypertrophy goals, anchoring training around two solid feedings is high-leverage and easy to comply with.

---

## Step 6 — Hydration & Micronutrients

- **Water:** 30–35 ml/kg baseline (~2.0–2.3 L) + 500–750 ml per training hour
- **Sodium:** don't restrict; aim for 3–5 g/day, more in hot weather/heavy sweating
- **Fibre:** 25–30 g/day from vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes
- **Calcium:** 1,000 mg/day — relevant given training loads and progestin-only/COC use; dairy or fortified alternatives 2–3 servings
- **Iron:** check status at baseline if she hasn't recently. COC tends to reduce menstrual blood loss, so iron status is typically better than off-pill — but recreational female lifters still under-consume. Red meat 1–2×/week or a multivitamin covers most cases.
- **Vitamin D:** 1,000–2,000 IU/day, especially if training indoors year-round

---

## Step 7 — Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Only)

| Supplement | Dose | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Creatine monohydrate | 5 g/day, any time | Strength, hypertrophy, recovery — most robust evidence |
| Whey protein | As needed to hit protein target | Convenience |
| Vitamin D3 | 1,000–2,000 IU | Insurance |
| Caffeine | 2–4 mg/kg pre-training, optional | Performance on heavy days; cap by 14:00 to protect sleep |
| Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) | 1–2 g/day | If oily fish intake is low |

Skip pre-workouts, fat burners, BCAAs (redundant if protein is hit), and testosterone boosters.

---

## Step 8 — Phase-Specific Nutrition Cues

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) — Build the Habit
- Focus on hitting protein every day before worrying about exact carb numbers
- Establish meal timing rhythm
- Weekly weigh-in average trend should be +0.2–0.3 kg/week by Week 3

### Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Fuel Heavier Training
- Push carbs slightly higher on Squat/Deadlift days (+30–50 g)
- Don't under-eat on Friday — Lower B on Thursday creates real recovery demand
- If sleep dips during Week 7 (heaviest accumulated load), add 20 g carbs to evening snack — improves sleep quality

### Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) — Performance Then Taper
- **Weeks 9–10:** Maintain surplus, prioritise sleep and stress management over fine-tuning macros
- **Week 11 (test week):** Eat to maintenance, prioritise carbs on testing days (lift days get +50 g pre-session). Hydrate aggressively the day before each test.
- **Week 12 (deload):** Drop ~150–200 kcal (mostly carbs since training volume crashes). This is the natural window to nibble off any fat gained during the surplus without compromising training adaptations.

---

## Step 9 — Tracking & Adjustments

**Weekly check-ins:**
- Average morning bodyweight (7 readings, drop the lowest and highest, average the middle 5)
- Training performance log (load × reps × RPE on primaries)
- Subjective: sleep quality, hunger, energy, mood — 1–10 scale

**Adjustment rules:**
- Weight static for 2 weeks AND training progressing → no change
- Weight static for 2 weeks AND training stalling → +150 kcal (carbs)
- Weight rising >0.4 kg/week consistently → –150 kcal (carbs/fat split)
- Energy/sleep tanking → check protein, carbs around training, and total kcal floor before assuming overtraining

**Photos/measurements:** every 4 weeks (end of each phase) — waist, hip, thigh, upper arm — more informative than scale alone.

---

## Practical Notes for the Client

- **Eating enough is the hardest part** of a hypertrophy block for most female recreational lifters. Expect resistance around the surplus — pre-empt it.
- **Don't fear carbs:** they're the primary training fuel and the easiest macro to scale up or down for adjustments.
- **Alcohol:** keep to ≤3 drinks/week during Phases 1–2, zero in Weeks 10–11. It blunts protein synthesis and sleep quality disproportionately in smaller individuals.
- **Travel/social meals:** hit protein and aim for "reasonable" — don't try to track everything. One imperfect day per week is irrelevant; one imperfect month is not.

---

If you can send me her actual bodyweight, height, occupation/daily activity level, and any food preferences or restrictions, I'll rebuild the numbers with real figures rather than the 65 kg placeholder.

# Cardiovascular Conditioning — General Health Add-On

**Goal:** Improve aerobic base, cardiovascular health markers, and recovery capacity **without interfering with strength and hypertrophy adaptations.**

**Guiding principle:** Concurrent training works when cardio is (a) mostly low-intensity, (b) separated from lifting where possible, and (c) modality-matched to avoid local muscle fatigue conflicting with the next session.

---

## Weekly Cardio Targets

Aligned with WHO general health guidance (150 min moderate OR 75 min vigorous per week) plus light daily movement:

| Component | Frequency | Duration | Intensity |
|-----------|-----------|----------|-----------|
| Zone 2 (steady aerobic) | 2×/week | 25–35 min | RPE 3–4, conversational, ~60–70% HRmax |
| Higher-intensity interval session | 1×/week (Phase 1–2 only) | 15–20 min total | RPE 7–8 on work intervals |
| Daily steps | Every day | 8,000–10,000 | Background activity |
| Mobility/flow | 2×/week | 10–15 min | Low; recovery-oriented |

Total structured cardio: ~75–90 min/week. Well within the volume that supports — rather than blunts — hypertrophy.

---

## Weekly Schedule (integrated with lifting)

| Day | Lifting | Cardio | Notes |
|-----|---------|--------|-------|
| Mon | Lower A | — | Don't add anything to leg day |
| Tue | Upper A | Zone 2, 25–30 min PM (bike or incline walk) | 6+ hr after lift if possible |
| Wed | Off | Intervals, 15–20 min + 10 min mobility | Main conditioning day |
| Thu | Lower B | — | Protect deadlift recovery |
| Fri | Upper B | Zone 2, 25–30 min PM | Same separation rule as Tue |
| Sat | Off | Long easy walk 45–60 min (counts as Zone 2) + mobility | Outdoor, social, low-stress |
| Sun | Off | Full rest or gentle walk | Recovery priority |

**Total weekly:** ~80 min structured Zone 2 + ~15 min intervals + walking. Hits the WHO floor with margin.

---

## Modality Selection

- **Zone 2:** incline treadmill walk (10–12% grade, 5–6 km/h), stationary bike, elliptical, easy rowing. Avoid running for primary Zone 2 work — eccentric load on legs interferes with squat/DL recovery in a recreational lifter.
- **Intervals:** bike or rower preferred. Both are low-impact and quad-dominant in a way that doesn't clash with hip-hinge recovery. Avoid sprinting on flat ground (hamstring risk, DOMS).
- **Walking:** outdoor, any pace that allows conversation. Steps are the single highest-leverage health intervention outside of sleep.

---

## Interval Session Templates (rotate weekly)

Pick one for the Wednesday slot. Warm up 5 min easy, cool down 5 min easy.

**Option A — Bike, 10×1 (Phase 1):**
- 1 min hard (RPE 7) / 1 min easy × 10
- Total work: 10 min

**Option B — Rower, 6×2 (Phase 2):**
- 2 min strong (RPE 7–8) / 2 min easy × 6

To minimise the "interference effect" between cardio and strength:

1. **Same-day rule:** if cardio and lifting must happen on the same day, lift first, separated by ≥6 hours where possible.
2. **Never** schedule intervals within 24 hours of a heavy lower-body session. Wednesday slot is deliberately between Mon Lower A and Thu Lower B but uses bike/rower to avoid eccentric leg damage.
3. **Cardio fuelling:** Zone 2 can be done fed or fasted, athlete preference. Intervals: always fuelled — at minimum a small carb feed 60–90 min prior.
4. **If sleep, joint feel, or lifting performance drop:** the cardio is the first thing to reduce, not the lifting.

# HIIT Day Add-On — Recommendation Against (and How to Do It If You Still Want To)

Before I build it: **I'd push back on adding a HIIT day to this programme.** Here's the reasoning, then the implementation if you want it anyway.

---

## Why I'd Recommend Against It

You just asked me to intensify Phase 2 because she's a good responder. The revised Phase 2 already includes:

- 5 lifting sessions' worth of high-RPE work compressed into 4 days
- RPE 9 top sets in Wk 7 on squat, bench, OHP
- A heavy deadlift single in Wk 7
- Heavy second exposures on every main lift
- A calorie surplus and 8+ hours of sleep as **prerequisites**, not nice-to-haves

Adding HIIT layers a second high-stress, glycolytic, CNS-taxing stimulus onto a programme that's already pushed to the edge of what concurrent training tolerates. The likely outcomes:

1. **Interference effect amplifies.** The research on concurrent training is reasonably clear: high-intensity cardio within ~24 h of heavy lower-body lifting blunts strength and hypertrophy adaptations. Z2 doesn't. HIIT does.
2. **Recovery debt accumulates silently.** Good responders often don't *feel* the cost until performance drops in Wk 7 or Wk 10 — exactly when you need the response.
3. **The original cardio prescription already covers HIIT-equivalent health benefits.** The Wednesday interval session in Phase 1 (and Wk 5 of Phase 2) is HIIT in everything but name. The reason I removed it from Wk 6 onward in the intensified Phase 2 was specifically to protect the lifting stimulus.
4. **It crowds the week.** She has 4 lifting days, 2 Z2 sessions, walking, and mobility. A 5th hard session means either dropping recovery work or doubling up on a lifting day — both bad trades.

**If the goal is general health:** the existing programme exceeds WHO guidance and produces strong VO₂max gains via Z2 + the intervals already built in.
**If the goal is fat loss:** raise step count and trim 100–150 kcal — cheaper, lower-risk, more effective.
**If the goal is "she likes HIIT and will adhere better with it in the plan":** that's a legitimate reason, and below is how to do it with minimum damage.

---

## If You Want It Anyway — Minimum-Damage Implementation

### Placement: Saturday

The only viable slot. Reasoning:

- **Mon (Lower A) / Thu (Lower B):** off-limits — same-day or day-before HIIT wrecks squat/DL quality
- **Tue / Fri (Upper days):** HIIT after upper lifting is *possible* but cuts into Z2 slots already there
- **Wed:** too close to Thu Lower B — HIIT Tue night → Wed HIIT → Thu deadlift is three CNS hits in 48 h
- **Sat:** 48 h after Fri lift, 48 h before Mon lift. Maximum buffer. Replaces the long Saturday walk.
- **Sun:** keep as full rest; do not stack HIIT and short turnaround to Mon

### Session Design

**Duration:** 20–25 min total, including warm-up and cool-down
**Modality:** Bike or rower — **never running.** Eccentric leg load on Saturday compromises Monday's squat.
**Format:** Choose one per week; rotate.

| Option | Structure | Work:Rest | Total Work | Intent |
|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|--------|
| A | 8 × 30 s hard / 90 s easy | 1:3 | 4 min | Standard MICT-adjacent HIIT, lowest recovery cost |
| B | 6 × 1 min hard / 2 min easy | 1:2 | 6 min | Moderate cost, classic aerobic HIIT |
| C | 10 × 20 s hard / 40 s easy (Tabata-adjacent) | 1:2 | ~3.5 min | Lowest time cost, highest RPE |

**Intensity:** RPE 8 on work intervals — *not* maximal. "Hard but I could have done one more interval." Going to RPE 9–10 on HIIT is where the interference cost spikes disproportionately.

Warm-up: 5 min easy + 2 build-up efforts. Cool-down: 5 min easy spin.

|-----|---------|--------------|
| Mon | Lower A | — |
| Tue | Upper A | Zone 2, 25 min PM |
| Wed | Off | Mobility 15 min + walk |

|-------|-------|-------------------|

HIIT on Saturday adds ~150–250 kcal of expenditure plus elevated post-exercise oxygen consumption. On HIIT days:

# Plyometric / Power Day — Recommendation Against, Firmly This Time

I have to push back harder here than I did on the HIIT request, because the trajectory of this programme is now actively working against itself. Let me lay it out honestly before answering the question.

---

## Where We Are

Over the course of this conversation, the programme has accumulated:

1. **Original 4-day Upper/Lower split** — already a full programme for a recreational lifter
2. **Intensified Phase 2** — RPE 9 top sets, heavy second exposures, AMRAPs, a heavy DL single in Wk 7
3. **Structured cardio** — 2× Z2, intervals, walking, mobility
4. **A HIIT day** — added against my recommendation, with mitigation built in

You're now asking to add a **fifth high-CNS, high-intensity stressor** on top of all of that, for a **recreational lifter** who hasn't started the programme yet and whose actual response to load is unknown — "good responder" is a hypothesis at this point, not a measured fact.

This is the pattern I'd flag for any trainer: each individual addition sounds reasonable, but the cumulative load has drifted well past what the original brief described (*"standard 12-week strength + hypertrophy programme"* for a *"recreational lifter"*). At this point I'd be doing you a disservice to keep saying yes and bolting things on.

---

## Why a Plyo/Power Day Is the Wrong Tool Here

**1. It doesn't serve the stated goal.** The brief is strength + hypertrophy. Plyometrics develop rate of force development and reactive strength — useful for athletes, sprinters, jumpers, court/field sport players. For a recreational lifter pursuing strength and hypertrophy, plyo contributes little to either adaptation that isn't already addressed by heavy compound lifting. The opportunity cost is real.

**2. CNS and connective tissue cost is high relative to the stimulus value.** Depth jumps, bounds, and high-intensity plyos are among the most neurally demanding things a person can do. They're typically programmed *in place of* heavy lower-body work on a given day, not in addition to it. Stacking them onto a programme with two heavy lower days plus deadlifts plus HIIT plus Z2 is how Achilles tendons, patellar tendons, and lower-back issues develop in lifters who were "fine" the week before.

**3. Recreational lifters generally lack the landing mechanics for true plyometric work.** Real plyometrics — depth jumps, reactive bounds — require coached landing technique. Without it, you're getting the injury risk without the adaptation. The plyos that are safe to self-coach (low pogos, light box jumps stepping down) are too low-intensity to justify a dedicated day.

**4. There's no free day to put it on.** Walk through the week:
   - Mon, Thu: heavy lower — plyo before kills the session, plyo after is neurally pointless and injury-prone
   - Tue, Fri: upper days — plyo turns these into double sessions
   - Wed: was the recovery/mobility buffer between lower days; now you want to put high-CNS lower-body work in the exact slot designed to dissipate lower-body fatigue
   - Sat: HIIT lives there now
   - Sun: the last remaining true recovery day

   There is no slot that doesn't compromise something already prescribed.

**5. Phase 3 risk.** The Wk 11 1RM tests are the payoff for the whole block. Plyometrics in Wk 9–10 substantially raise the risk of a tendon issue derailing the test week. Plyometrics in Wk 7 (already the highest-stress week) risks Phase 2 collapse.

---

## What I Think Is Actually Going On

A few possibilities — worth being honest about which one applies:

- **Scope creep from enthusiasm.** New client, you want to give her a comprehensive programme. Understandable, but more isn't better; *appropriate* is better.
- **The client is asking for variety.** If she's bored or wants more athletic-feeling training, that's solvable inside existing sessions, not with a new day.
- **You're programming for an athlete, not a recreational lifter.** If her actual goals include sport performance, jumping ability, or athleticism, that changes the entire programme structure — not by adding a day, but by rewriting from scratch.
- **Testing my willingness to keep saying yes.** Fair enough, and the answer is no.

---

## What I'd Do Instead

If the underlying want is *some* power/athletic quality without compromising the programme, here are three options ordered by how strongly I'd recommend them:

### Option 1 (Recommended): Power Primer Before Heavy Lower Days
Add **3–5 minutes of low-volume jumps** as part of the warm-up on Mon and Thu, before working sets of squat and deadlift. This is the standard, evidence-supported way to integrate power work into a strength block.

- **Mon (before squat):** 3 × 3 box jumps (step down, don't drop), moderate box height
- **Thu (before deadlift):** 3 × 3 broad jumps or 3 × 5 vertical jumps
- Total time: ~5 min added to warm-up
- Cost: negligible. Often improves the working sets via post-activation potentiation.

This gives you ~80% of the realistic benefit of a power day, for ~5% of the cost, with zero schedule disruption. **This is the answer.**

### Option 2: Convert One Existing Lower Day to a Power-Strength Hybrid (Phase 1 only)
If you specifically want a session that *feels* like a power day, restructure Lower B in Phase 1 only:

- Box Jump — 4 × 3 (full reset between reps)
- Trap Bar Jump (light, ~30% 1RM) — 4 × 3
- Conventional Deadlift — 3 × 5 @ RPE 7 (reduced volume vs. original)
- Front Squat — 3 × 6
- Single-leg work + posterior chain accessories as written

This swaps power work *in for* some lifting volume on a day already programmed for lower body, rather than adding a session. End it at Phase 1; return to standard Lower B for Phase 2 and beyond.

### Option 3: Remove Something First
If you genuinely want a dedicated power day, the programme has to make room. Realistic candidates:
- Drop the Saturday HIIT (which I already recommended against)
- Reduce to 3 lifting days/week and put plyometrics on the 4th
- Extend the programme to 16 weeks with a dedicated power block

I'd build any of these out properly if you want, but they're real restructures, not additions.

---

## My Recommendation

Take **Option 1**: 5 minutes of jumps as a primer before heavy lower days. It costs nothing, fits the existing programme, gives her the athletic feel and the rate-of-force-development stimulus, and doesn't put the Wk 11 test at risk.

If you tell me her goals are different from the original brief — she's training for a sport, she has athletic performance ambitions, she specifically wants vertical jump or sprint development — I'll rebuild the programme around that goal from the top, not patch power work onto a hypertrophy plan.

Which direction do you want to go?

# 1RM Test Protocol — End of Phase 3 (Week 11)

**Dates:** Monday 10 August – Friday 14 August 2026
**Purpose:** Quantify strength gains across the 12-week block on the four primary lifts: Back Squat, Bench Press, Conventional Deadlift, Overhead Press.

This is already built into the master programme as Week 11. Below is the detailed protocol — how to run each day, attempt selection, the week's structure, and how to interpret results.

---

## Pre-Test Preparation (Week 10 leading in)

The peaking week (Wk 10) already sets this up: heavy doubles at RPE 9, accessory volume cut ~50%, sleep and food prioritised. By the end of Wk 10 she should feel **sharp, slightly under-trained, and hungry to lift heavy** — not beat up.

### Final 72 Hours Before Each Test

- **Sleep:** 8+ hours each of the two nights before
- **Hydration:** 35–40 ml/kg + electrolytes daily; don't over-water test morning
- **Carbs:** add ~50 g to the dinner the night before each test
- **Caffeine:** if she uses it, 3–6 mg/kg 45–60 min pre-test; if she doesn't, **don't introduce it now**
- **No new variables on test day:** no new shoes, no new belt, no new pre-workout, no first-time lifting straps. Everything she uses she's used before.
- **No alcohol** during the entire test week
- **No extra training:** no plyo primers, no extra accessory work, no "feeling it out" the day before — Wk 11 schedule is the schedule

---

## Week 11 Schedule

| Day | Date | Session | Notes |
|-----|------|---------|-------|
| Mon | 10 Aug | **Back Squat 1RM test** | Highest CNS demand first when fresh |
| Tue | 11 Aug | **Bench Press 1RM test** | Upper body, low overlap with Mon |
| Wed | 12 Aug | Off — walk + mobility only | Critical recovery day |
| Thu | 13 Aug | **Conventional Deadlift 1RM test** | 48 h after squat = minimum acceptable gap |
| Fri | 14 Aug | **Overhead Press 1RM test** + light pulling | Lowest absolute load; pair with easy back work |
| Sat/Sun | 15–16 Aug | Full rest | Lead into Wk 12 deload |

### Why this order?
- **Squat first:** highest neural demand; needs maximum freshness
- **Bench second:** minimal lower-body overlap; allows squat recovery
- **48 h gap then deadlift:** the deadlift is the most fatiguing test; the Wed off-day is non-negotiable
- **OHP last:** lowest absolute load, easiest to recover into, smallest stakes if she's accumulated some fatigue

Do **not** compress this to 2 or 3 days. Trainers sometimes try to test bench + OHP same day, or squat + deadlift same day. The numbers come in lower, and the data becomes less useful. Four days, one lift each.

---

## Per-Test Warm-Up & Attempt Selection

### General Warm-Up (each day)
1. 5 min easy bike or row
2. 5 min targeted mobility (hips/ankles before squat/DL; T-spine/shoulders before bench/OHP)
3. Empty bar — 2 × 8, slow and controlled

### Specific Warm-Up — Ramp to Opener

Use percentages of her **best estimated 1RM** going into the test. Estimate this from Wk 10's heavy double using the formula **double × 1.06** as a starting point, then cross-check against Wk 9's RPE 8.5 triples (triple ÷ 0.92).

The ramp:

| Set | Load (%est 1RM) | Reps | Rest |
|-----|----------------|------|------|
| 1 | 50% | 5 | 2 min |
| 2 | 65% | 3 | 2–3 min |
| 3 | 75% | 2 | 3 min |
| 4 | 85% | 1 | 3–4 min |
| 5 | 92% | 1 | 4–5 min |
| **Opener** | **~95% of est 1RM** | **1** | **4–5 min** |
| **Second attempt** | **~100% of est 1RM** | **1** | **5 min** |
| **Third attempt** | **102–105% of est 1RM** | **1** | **—** |

### Attempt Selection Logic

This is borrowed from powerlifting practice because it works.

- **Opener (~95%):** should feel like an RPE 8 single — fast, no grind, technically clean. If the opener grinds, **don't go up; repeat it or stop.** The opener tells you whether the test day is a green light or a yellow flag.
- **Second attempt (~100% of estimate):** matches or matches-plus-small-jump on the estimated 1RM. RPE 9 — hard, may slow at sticking point, but moves with intent.
- **Third attempt:** the actual PR attempt. Size of jump depends on how the second moved:
  - Second moved like RPE 8.5 → jump 2.5–5 kg upper, 5–7.5 kg lower

- Bench, OHP: 2.5 kg jumps available (use 1.25 kg plates if she's close to a round number target)
- Squat, Deadlift: 5 kg jumps standard; 2.5 kg if a smaller jump is what makes the lift

### Monday — Back Squat
- **Equipment:** her normal squat shoes, belt for sets ≥85%, knee sleeves optional but use what she used in training

- **Spotters / safety:** safety bars set at just-below-bottom position. Two human spotters or solo with safeties properly set. **Do not test without one or the other.**
- **Tempo:** controlled descent, no bounce, drive up on intent

### Tuesday — Bench Press
- **Equipment:** her normal grip width, wrist wraps if used in training, no slingshot/board work
- **Standard:** pause on chest (~1 s), no heave, butt stays on bench, feet stay planted
- **Safety:** spotter mandatory for second and third attempts. A handoff is allowed and recommended on heavy attempts.
- **Tempo:** controlled descent, paused, pressed to lockout

### Thursday — Conventional Deadlift
- **Equipment:** belt for sets ≥85%, chalk, her normal footwear (flat-soled). Straps **not allowed** for the test — grip is part of the lift.
- **Standard:** locked knees, hips through, shoulders behind the bar at lockout. No hitching.
- **Style:** whatever she trained — conventional throughout the block, so conventional on test day. **Don't switch to sumo for the test.**
- **Reset between reps not relevant — singles only**
- **Special note:** the third deadlift attempt is the highest-injury-risk attempt of the week. If form breaks down meaningfully on the second attempt, **don't take a third**. Take the second as the PR.

### Friday — Overhead Press
- **Equipment:** belt optional, wrist wraps if used
- **Standard:** strict press from the front rack, no leg drive, no layback beyond normal pressing arch, lockout overhead with biceps by ears
- **No push press substitution.** If she misses the third attempt, the test is the strict OHP number.

- Between ramp-up sets: as written above (2–5 min)

### Baseline for Comparison
Use the **estimated 1RMs from Wk 1** as the reference, calculated from her top working sets in Wk 1 via:
- 6-rep set: load ÷ 0.86
- 8-rep set: load ÷ 0.80

If you didn't capture this in Wk 1, use her stated lifetime PRs at programme start. This is why I emphasised logging from Wk 1.

### Expected Gains Over 12 Weeks (recreational lifter, good responder, fed and recovered)

| Lift | Realistic gain | Strong outcome |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| Squat | +7.5–15 kg | +15–20 kg |
| Bench | +5–10 kg | +10–12.5 kg |
| Deadlift | +10–17.5 kg | +20 kg |
| OHP | +2.5–7.5 kg | +7.5–10 kg |

If she hits "strong outcome" range across all four, the intensified Phase 2 paid off. If she hits "realistic gain" range, the programme worked as designed. If she's below realistic on multiple lifts, the diagnosis is almost always: (1) sleep was insufficient, (2) calories were under target, or (3) RPE was misreported during training — in roughly that order.

### Red Flags in the Data
- **Opener feels heavy (>RPE 8) on multiple days** → she came into test week under-recovered. The PRs that follow are likely 2.5–5 kg below true capacity. Note this; don't write off the block.
- **Big PR on one lift, flat on others** → likely a specificity or technique issue on the flat lift, not a programming failure. Useful info for the next block.
- **PR on bench/OHP, flat on squat/DL** → almost always under-fuelled. Lower body responds most to calorie surplus.

# Full 12-Week Programme Summary

**Client:** 26F, recreational lifter, on COC (no cycle phasing required), fully cleared for full intensity
**Dates:** Monday 1 June 2026 – Sunday 23 August 2026
**Structure:** 4 lifting days/week (Upper/Lower split) + cardio for general health
**Goals:** Strength + hypertrophy, with 1RM tests in Wk 11

---

## Programme at a Glance

| Phase | Weeks | Dates | Focus | Primary Rep Range | Top RPE |
|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------------------|---------|
| 1. Hypertrophy Accumulation | 1–4 | 1 Jun – 28 Jun | Volume, work capacity, technique | 5–8 on primaries | 7–8 |
| 2. Strength Emphasis (intensified) | 5–8 | 29 Jun – 26 Jul | Heavy compounds, second exposures | 2–3 on primaries | 8.5–9 |
| 3. Peak / Test / Deload | 9–12 | 27 Jul – 23 Aug | Intensification → 1RM tests → recovery | 1–3, then taper | 9 → light |

---

## Weekly Structure (constant across the block)

| Day | Session | Cardio |
|-----|---------|--------|
| Mon | Lower A (squat-focused) | — |
| Tue | Upper A (bench-focused) | Zone 2, 25–30 min PM |
| Wed | Off | Mobility 15 min + walk; intervals in Phase 1 only |
| Thu | Lower B (deadlift-focused) | — |
| Fri | Upper B (press/pull) | Zone 2, 25–30 min PM |
| Sat | Off | Long walk 45–60 min + mobility |
| Sun | Off | Full rest or gentle walk |

**Power primer (Mon + Thu):** 3 × 3 box jumps before squat, 3 × 3 broad jumps before deadlift. ~5 min, part of warm-up.

---

## PHASE 1 — Hypertrophy Accumulation (Weeks 1–4)

### Lower A — Monday
- Back Squat — 4 × 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Romanian Deadlift — 3 × 8–10 @ RPE 7
- Walking Lunge — 3 × 10/leg
- Leg Press — 3 × 12
- Standing Calf Raise — 4 × 10–12
- Hanging Knee Raise — 3 × 12

### Upper A — Tuesday
- Bench Press — 4 × 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-Supported Row — 4 × 8–10
- DB Shoulder Press — 3 × 8–10
- Lat Pulldown — 3 × 10–12
- DB Lateral Raise — 3 × 12–15
- EZ-Bar Curl — 3 × 10
- Triceps Rope Pressdown — 3 × 12

### Lower B — Thursday
- Conventional Deadlift — 3 × 5 @ RPE 7
- Front Squat — 3 × 8 @ RPE 7
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 × 8/leg
- Hamstring Curl — 4 × 10–12
- Hip Thrust — 3 × 10
- Seated Calf Raise — 4 × 12
- Cable Crunch — 3 × 12

### Upper B — Friday
- Overhead Press — 4 × 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Pull-Up (assisted PRN) — 4 × AMRAP-2
- Incline DB Press — 3 × 10
- Seated Cable Row — 3 × 10–12
- Face Pull — 3 × 15
- Hammer Curl — 3 × 10
- Overhead Triceps Extension — 3 × 12

### Phase 1 Progression
- **Wk 1 (1–7 Jun):** Establish loads at top of rep range, RPE 7. Log everything.
- **Wk 2 (8–14 Jun):** +2.5% upper / +5% lower on primaries; +1 rep on accessories where possible.
- **Wk 3 (15–21 Jun):** Push primaries to RPE 8; add a 4th set to one accessory per session.
- **Wk 4 (22–28 Jun):** Light deload — primaries 3 × 5 @ ~70% of Wk 3, RPE 6; accessory sets cut ~40%. Drop Wed intervals.

### Phase 1 Cardio
- Tue + Fri PM: Zone 2, 25–30 min
- Wed: 15–20 min intervals (bike or rower, 10 × 1 min or 6 × 2 min) + mobility
- Sat: 45–60 min walk + mobility
- Daily: 8–10k steps

---

## PHASE 2 — Strength Emphasis, Intensified (Weeks 5–8)

### Lower A — Monday
- Back Squat — 5 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Pause Back Squat — 2 × 3 @ ~85% of top set
- Romanian Deadlift — 4 × 5 @ RPE 8
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 × 6/leg, loaded
- Leg Extension — 3 × 10
- Standing Calf Raise — 4 × 8
- Hanging Leg Raise — 3 × 10

### Upper A — Tuesday
- Bench Press — 5 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Close-Grip Bench — 3 × 5 @ RPE 8
- Pendlay Row — 4 × 5 @ RPE 8
- Weighted Pull-Up — 4 × 5
- DB Lateral Raise — 4 × 10
- Incline DB Curl — 3 × 8

### Lower B — Thursday
- Conventional Deadlift — 4 × 2 @ RPE 8.5
- Deficit Deadlift (1") — 3 × 3 @ RPE 7.5
- Front Squat — 3 × 5 @ RPE 8
- Hip Thrust — 4 × 6 @ RPE 8
- Glute-Ham Raise (or Nordic) — 3 × 6–8
- Seated Calf Raise — 4 × 10
- Cable Crunch — 3 × 10

### Upper B — Friday
- Overhead Press — 5 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Push Press — 3 × 3 @ RPE 8
- Weighted Pull-Up — 4 × 5
- Incline Bench Press — 4 × 6 @ RPE 8
- Chest-Supported Row — 3 × 8
- Cable Lateral Raise — 3 × 12
- Skullcrusher — 3 × 8

### Phase 2 Progression
- **Wk 5 (29 Jun – 5 Jul):** Reset primaries to ~87.5% of est 1RM for 5 × 3. Heavy variants at conservative loads. Keep one interval session.
- **Wk 6 (6–12 Jul):** +2.5% upper / +5% lower on primaries. Final top set of Squat/Bench/OHP becomes AMRAP at prescribed load. No deadlift AMRAP. Drop intervals from here on.
- **Wk 7 (13–19 Jul):** **Peak intensity.** Top sets at RPE 9 on Squat/Bench/OHP. Deadlift: work to heavy single @ RPE 9, then 2 × 2 @ 90%. No AMRAPs. Highest-stress week until Wk 10 — extra food, extra sleep, drop one Z2 session.
- **Wk 8 (20–26 Jul):** Modified back-off. Primaries 4 × 3 @ RPE 7.5. Heavy variants removed. Accessories -10% intensity. Resume both Z2 sessions.

---

## PHASE 3 — Peak / Test / Deload (Weeks 9–12)

### Week 9 — Intensification (27 Jul – 2 Aug)
- Back Squat — 3 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Bench Press — 4 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Deadlift — 3 × 3 @ RPE 8
- Overhead Press — 4 × 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Accessories: Phase 2 template, cut to 2 sets each
- Cardio: 2× Zone 2, no intervals

### Week 10 — Peaking (3–9 Aug)
- Back Squat — Work up to heavy double @ RPE 9; back-off 2 × 3 @ 85%
- Bench — Heavy double @ RPE 9; 2 × 3 @ 85%
- Deadlift — Heavy double @ RPE 9
- OHP — Heavy double @ RPE 9
- Accessory volume cut ~50%
- Cardio: 1× Zone 2 (20 min) + walking only

### Week 11 — Test Week (10–14 Aug)

| Day | Date | Test |
|-----|------|------|
| Mon | 10 Aug | Back Squat 1RM |
| Tue | 11 Aug | Bench Press 1RM |
| Wed | 12 Aug | Off — walk + mobility |
| Thu | 13 Aug | Conventional Deadlift 1RM |
| Fri | 14 Aug | Overhead Press 1RM + light pulling |

**Ramp on each test day:** 50% × 5 → 65% × 3 → 75% × 2 → 85% × 1 → 92% × 1 → Opener (~95%) → Second (~100% est) → Third (102–105%). Rest 4–5 min between heavy singles.

**Rules:** Opener must feel RPE 8 or test is yellow-flagged. If second attempt grinds, stop — don't take a third. Spotters/safeties mandatory on squat and bench. No straps on deadlift. Strict OHP only.

**Record:** bodyweight AM, all attempts + RPE, video of heaviest success, subjective wellness 1–10.

Cardio Wk 11: walking only. No structured sessions.

### Week 12 — Deload (17–23 Aug)
- 3 short sessions (skip 4th)
- All primary lifts: 60% × 3 × 3, technical focus
- Accessories: 2 × 10 @ RPE 5 or skipped
- Cardio: 2× Zone 2 (25–30 min) + 1 light interval session
- Priority: walking, mobility, sleep, food at maintenance –100 to –200 kcal

## Programme Rules

**Autoregulation:**

- Subjective wellness ≤4 on two markers → drop one RPE point that session

**Monitoring (weekly):**
- AM bodyweight, 7 readings, drop high/low, average middle 5
- Training log: load × reps × RPE on all working sets
- Sleep, hunger, energy, mood (1–10)
- Photos + waist/hip/thigh/arm at end of each phase

- Power primer is part of warm-up only, not a separate session

- Week 11 schedule is the schedule; no extra training in test week
- Week 12 deload happens even if she feels good post-PRs
